items.stem: A 38-year-old patient becomes dizzy and disoriented two minutes after an inadvertent high dose of local anesthetic during a regional block. The patient reports a metallic taste and numbness around the mouth.
items.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?

A.text: Symptoms beginning immediately after local-anesthetic exposure, especially metallic taste, circumoral numbness, and disorientation, support early systemic toxicity.

B.text: Pallor, bradycardia, and hypotension after a needle stimulus without the characteristic neurologic prodrome.

C.text: Prominent tachypnea and anxiety with paresthesias, without a toxic temporal dose relationship.

D.text: Palpitations, tremor, and hypertension immediately after an epinephrine-containing injection without neurologic toxicity.

items.stem: A 72-year-old patient has progressive exertional dyspnea and a newly recognized harsh systolic murmur. Blood pressure and oxygen saturation are stable.
items.lead_in: Which investigation is most appropriate to characterize the suspected valve lesion and its hemodynamic consequences?

B.text: Echocardiography directly identifies the affected valve, grades lesion severity, and evaluates ventricular and hemodynamic consequences.

A.text: Useful for rhythm or chamber-strain assessment, but it does not define valve anatomy or lesion severity.

C.text: Useful for pulmonary congestion or gross cardiac silhouette, but it does not characterize valve severity.

D.text: Can support heart-failure assessment, but it does not identify and grade the valve lesion.

items.stem: A 39-year-old patient has a 2-cm uterine fibroid found incidentally. Menstrual bleeding is normal, hemoglobin is normal, there are no pressure symptoms, and the patient has no fertility concerns.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate management?

C.text: Asymptomatic fibroids generally require no treatment; intervention is selected for symptoms and patient goals.

A.text: Appropriate for selected symptomatic patients who want uterine or fertility preservation.

B.text: Appropriate for selected symptomatic patients desiring uterine preservation but not future fertility.

D.text: Definitive treatment for substantial symptoms when fertility and uterine preservation are not desired.

items.stem: A healthy patient at 28 weeks' gestation presents for routine antenatal care. Routine vaccines were up to date before pregnancy, and there is no vaccine-specific contraindication.
items.lead_in: Which vaccination action is most appropriate at this visit?

options.text: Defer Tdap until after delivery because it was received previously

D.text: Tdap is recommended during every pregnancy, ideally at 27–32 weeks, regardless of prior Tdap history.

A.text: Appropriate when indicated outside pregnancy; it is a live vaccine and is contraindicated during pregnancy.

B.text: Appropriate for susceptible nonpregnant patients; it is a live vaccine and is contraindicated during pregnancy.

C.text: Postpartum Tdap is used when it was missed in pregnancy, but prior history does not replace Tdap in each pregnancy.

items.stem: An immunocompetent 18-month-old child is due for routine vaccines. The child has mild rhinorrhea and a temperature of 37.6°C, is drinking normally, and has no history of vaccine allergy.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate vaccination plan?

options.text: Defer vaccination until a moderate or severe acute illness improves
Withhold the implicated vaccine after confirmed anaphylaxis to a component
Delay live vaccines during substantial immunosuppression

A.text: A mild illness, with or without a low fever, is not a reason to delay routine immunization in an otherwise eligible child.

B.text: Correct when acute illness is moderate or severe, rather than mild.

C.text: Correct when there is confirmed anaphylaxis to that vaccine or a constituent.

D.text: Correct when the child has a clinically important immunocompromising condition or therapy.

items.stem: A 3-year-old child has acute watery diarrhea and mildly dry mucous membranes. The child is alert, has normal perfusion, is not vomiting, and drinks eagerly.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate initial treatment?

options.text: Continue usual fluids without a structured rehydration plan

B.text: Mild dehydration with preserved perfusion and ability to drink is treated initially with oral rehydration solution.

A.text: Correct for shock, severe dehydration, or failure of safe enteral rehydration.

C.text: Appropriate when vomiting prevents oral rehydration in an eligible child.

D.text: Reasonable when dehydration is absent; it is insufficient for established dehydration.

items.stem: A report states that Region A recorded 600 new cases of a disease last year and Region B recorded 400. It gives no population sizes or person-time denominators.

options.text: Region A necessarily had the higher incidence rate
Region B necessarily had the lower disease prevalence
The rates cannot be compared without the population denominators
The two regions had equivalent risk because both reported counts

C.text: Counts alone do not establish rates; the defined population or person-time denominator is required.

A.text: Correct only if the relevant population or person-time denominators and ascertainment were equivalent.

B.text: A prevalence comparison would require defined populations and existing-case counts, not these new-case counts alone.

D.text: Equivalence could be assessed only after comparable rate denominators and uncertainty were supplied.

blind_solve.best_answer: The rates cannot be compared without the population denominators

items.stem: The same therapy reduces event risk from 20% to 10% in Population A and from 2% to 1% in Population B. The relative risk reduction is 50% in both, but the number needed to treat is 10 in A and 100 in B.
items.lead_in: What best explains the different numbers needed to treat?

options.text: The treatment has different relative effects
The studies used different diagnostic-test specificities
The result is explained by randomization failure
The populations have different baseline event risks

D.text: NNT is the reciprocal of absolute risk reduction. The same relative reduction creates a larger absolute reduction when baseline risk is higher.

A.text: Could explain different absolute effects if relative risk reductions differed, but they are explicitly identical here.

B.text: Could alter observed event classification, but no measurement difference is described.

C.text: Confounding could distort an effect in a nonrandom comparison, but it is neither needed nor supported to explain the arithmetic shown.

blind_solve.best_answer: The populations have different baseline event risks

items.stem: A 32-year-old patient says they intend to die tonight, describes a specific plan, has access to the means, and cannot agree to remain safe. No reliable support person is available.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate immediate disposition?

options.text: Maintain continuous observation and arrange emergency psychiatric assessment
Discharge with a written safety plan and follow-up within one week
Arrange urgent outpatient psychiatry within 48 hours
Ask family to supervise at home and remove lethal means

A.text: Current intent, a specific plan, means access, and inability to maintain safety require a secure setting, continuous observation, and emergency assessment.

B.text: Appropriate only for substantially lower acute risk with a feasible collaborative safety plan and reliable follow-up.

C.text: Can fit elevated but non-imminent risk when immediate safety is secured outside hospital.

D.text: May contribute to a lower-risk community plan when reliable supports exist, but it is insufficient here.

blind_solve.best_answer: Maintain continuous observation and arrange emergency psychiatric assessment

items.stem: A patient with moderate-to-severe opioid use disorder requests maintenance treatment. They value a lower overdose risk and flexible take-home dosing, and there is no contraindication to buprenorphine initiation.
items.lead_in: Which medication is the preferred first-line choice?

B.text: Buprenorphine/naloxone is preferred first-line when appropriate and fits the stated priorities because of its safety and access advantages.

A.text: An evidence-based opioid agonist alternative when buprenorphine is unsuitable or ineffective, or patient factors favour methadone.

C.text: An alternative when first-line opioid agonist treatments are contraindicated, unavailable, or ineffective.

D.text: May suit a fully withdrawn patient who specifically prefers antagonist treatment and can start it safely.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man has a small, easily reducible inguinal hernia found on examination. It causes no pain or activity limitation, and there are no obstructive symptoms.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate management strategy?

C.text: Watchful waiting is a safe option for carefully selected patients with an asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic inguinal hernia.

A.text: Appropriate for a symptomatic elective inguinal hernia when operative treatment is chosen.

B.text: Appropriate for selected symptomatic patients or circumstances favouring a minimally invasive approach.

D.text: Required for suspected strangulation, incarceration, or bowel obstruction.

items.stem: A 24-year-old patient has lateral ankle pain after an inversion injury. There is no tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus, and the patient can walk four steps.
items.lead_in: What is the most appropriate imaging decision?

options.text: No ankle imaging is indicated now

D.text: The Ottawa ankle rules are negative, so routine ankle radiography is not indicated; advanced imaging is also unnecessary initially.

A.text: Correct when the Ottawa ankle rules are positive for malleolar tenderness or inability to bear weight.

B.text: May be appropriate later for persistent symptoms or suspected occult or complex soft-tissue injury.

C.text: May be appropriate for a focused tendon question, not routine initial assessment of this uncomplicated sprain.

blind_solve.best_answer: No ankle imaging is indicated now

canonical_machine_audit.method: Every artifact is scanned for the longest run of consecutive tokens also occurring in the locally indexed Toronto Notes corpus, seeded on 12-word matches. The fingerprint set is built in memory and never written.
